tools.name: check_email
tools.description: Check one email address against the disposable-email-domains list (CC0): disposable (domain or a parent domain is listed), role address (info@, admin@ …), free webmail provider, look-alike (confusable) domain, practical syntax, and a one-character typo suggestion for big webmail domains. List-based

tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Check a domain only (no local part; anything containing "@" is refused): disposable (the domain or a parent domain is on the disposable-email-domains list), free webmail provider, look-alike (confusable) domain and a typo suggestion. Use this when you do not need the part before the @. Read-only. Sa

tools.name: get_meta
tools.description: Return the service version and build, the disposable-list version, domain and allowlist counts, the last refresh time, the upstream source and licence (CC0), and the current limits. Does not count as a check. Read-only. Same data as GET /v1/meta.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_email, check_domain · Public sink: check_email, check_domain · Destructive: check_email.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_email, check_domain · Public sink: check_email, check_domain · Destructive: check_email

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
